title: ContentPostureDraft7
description: Issue #115: the content vocabulary under the one dialect that asserts it. Each position must carry the check, and none of them may narrow the Go type -- a number satisfies a content keyword trivially, so the wrapper keeps a non-string value verbatim and its Validate returns early.

blob.$comment: No declared type. This is the shape that resolved to `any`, which Go forbids methods on, so nothing was checked anywhere.

doc.$comment: A declared string. The check has to be the same one the typeless spelling gets, written by the same code.

encodedDoc.$comment: Both keywords: contentMediaType judges the bytes contentEncoding produced, so the two are one check and not two.

unknownEncoding.$comment: An encoding nothing here decides. Carried as an annotation rather than guessed at, so every string satisfies it -- but the property still gets a type with a Validate.

boundedBlob.$comment: A length bound beside the content keywords, which is about the same string: one wrapper carries both.

list.$comment: An element position. The element's Go type is a plain string, so there is no named type to hang the check on and it rides the per-element rules -- which is where the identical subschema written as a property was checked and this one was not.

viaAllOf.$comment: A branch stating only a content keyword. The merge has to carry it, or the merged schema has nothing left to name a type from and falls through to `any`.

branch.$comment: Issue #183: a oneOf branch. Selection resolved the branch to a bare Go string, which carries no Validate for the union's dispatch to call, so the encoding was asserted nowhere -- while the identical subschema written as a plain property was checked.

tuple.$comment: The same reduction at the tuple slot, in the draft 4-7 spelling this document is written in: the position fell back to testing the JSON type, which answered "string" -- true, and silent about the encoding.
